questions.text: Which of the given number has its IEEE-754 32-bit floating point representation as (0 10000000 110 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000)
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Sign = 0 (positive)
- Exponent = 10000000 = 128 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 128 [latex]-[/latex] 127 = 1
- Mantissa = 1.11 (binary) = 1.75

Value = [latex]1.75\times2^1=3.5[/latex]

Answer: 3.5

questions.text: The total number of prime implicants of the function f(w,x,y,z)=[latex]\Sigma[/latex](0,2,4,5,6,10) is _______.
questions.solution:
Minterms 0, 2, 4, 5, 6, 10. From the K-map, the prime implicants are:

- [latex]\bar w\bar z[/latex] (0, 2, 4, 6)
- [latex]\bar wx\bar y[/latex] (4, 5)
- [latex]\bar xy\bar z[/latex] (2, 10)

Answer: 3

questions.text: Consider the equation [latex](43)_{x}=(y3)_{8}[/latex] where x and y are unknown. The number of possible solutions is ______________
questions.solution:
[latex](43)_x=4x+3,\quad(y3)_8=8y+3\Rightarrow x=2y[/latex]

Digit 4 needs x [latex]\ge[/latex] 5 and y must be an octal digit (0 to 7). So y = 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 5 solutions.

Answer: 5

questions.text:
Given the function F=P'+QR , where F is a function in three Boolean variables P,Q and R and P'=!P, consider the following statements.
(S1) F=[latex]\Sigma[/latex](4,5,6)
(S2) F=[latex]\Sigma[/latex](0,1,2,3,7)
(S3) F=[latex]\Pi[/latex](4,5,6)
(S4) F=[latex]\Pi[/latex](0,1,2,3,7)
Which of the following is true?
questions.solution:
F = P' + QR is 1 for P = 0 (minterms 0, 1, 2, 3) and for P = Q = R = 1 (minterm 7).

- [latex]F=\Sigma(0,1,2,3,7)[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] S2 True, S1 False
- Maxterms are the rest: [latex]F=\Pi(4,5,6)[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] S3 True, S4 False

Answer: (S1) False, (S2) True, (S3) True, (S4) False

questions.text:
Let # be a binary operator defined as
X#Y=X'+Y' where X and Y are Boolean variables.
Consider the following two statements.

(S1) (P # Q) # R = P # (Q # R)
(S2) Q # R = R # Q

Which of the following is/are true for the Boolean variables P, Q and R?
questions.solution:
X # Y = X' + Y' = (XY)', i.e. NAND.

- S2: NAND is commutative [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- S1: (P # Q) # R = PQ + R', while P # (Q # R) = P' + QR. Different (e.g. P = 0, R = 1) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False

Answer: Only S2 is true
